question.prompt: What is the tens digit of \(7^{2011}?\)

solutions.explanation:
To find the tens digit, track the last two digits of successive powers. When multiplying by \(7\), any whole hundreds contribute another multiple of \(100\), so only the previous last two digits affect the next last two digits.

The first four powers are
\[
7^1=7,\quad 7^2=49,\quad
7^3=343,\quad 7^4=2401.
\]
Their last two digits are \(07,49,43,01\). Multiplying a number ending in \(01\) by \(7\) produces one ending in \(07\), returning to the first pair. Since each next pair is determined by the current pair, the cycle repeats every four powers.

Now
\[
2011=4\cdot502+3.
\]
After \(502\) complete cycles, the exponent is at the third position, whose last two digits are \(43\). Therefore the tens digit is \(4\), choice D.
solutions.title: Track the last two digits
